themes.label: Concentrated AI rule-making widens inequality
themes.definition: Concern that AI infrastructure, knowledge and rule-making concentrated in a few countries will widen inequality, with developing nations demanding a role in setting standards.
themes.inclusion: Passages warning about AI concentration in a few countries or demanding developing-country participation in AI standard-setting.
themes.exclusion: General statements of AI benefit without concentration or participation claims.
themes.boundary_cases: Overlaps with digital divide; code here when concentration of rule-making or infrastructure is explicit.

examples.quote: It can also widen the inequality if infrastructure, knowledge, and rule-making remains concentrated in a few countries.
Developing nations must help shape the standards that will govern technologies affecting their people.

themes.label: AI improving education, health, agriculture
themes.definition: AI presented as able to improve sectors such as education, health, agriculture and public administration, and to accelerate development.
themes.inclusion: Passages listing development sectors AI can improve or opportunities to accelerate development.
themes.exclusion: Passages only about risk or governance.
themes.boundary_cases: Development benefit framed within a GDC principle may also be coded AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence can improve, of course, education, health, agriculture, and public administration.

themes.label: Global Digital Compact principles on AI
themes.definition: Endorsement of the Global Digital Compact's principles on safe, secure and trustworthy AI for development.
themes.inclusion: Passages welcoming Global Digital Compact or Pact for the Future provisions on AI.
themes.boundary_cases: If the GDC is named without any AI or technology content, do not code.

examples.quote: We welcome the Global Digital Compact’s principle of ensuring safe, secure and trustworthy emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence

value.rationale: Sierra Leone passages frame AI as a development opportunity whose benefits depend on inclusive governance; 2026 stresses concentration of AI rule-making in a few countries, while 2024 endorses the Global Digital Compact.
